messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the slot-lease RFC — I sketched a concrete lifecycle + cooldown proposal for dedicated pools. Wanted to surface it here before I open an RFC PR.

kevin: nice, curious how you handled queued requests vs credit drains.

sophie: can you paste the short config example? makes it easier to reason about.

maria: sure. core idea: leases have a soft and hard lifecycle. soft=grace (can be reclaimed with gentle eviction), hard=force reclaim after cooldown windows. we also track per-tenant lease credits that decay on use and slowly replenish. quick config: 

```
autoscaler:
  lease_soft_ttl_sec: 300
  lease_hard_ttl_sec: 1800
  lease_cooldown_sec: 120
  tenant_credit_replenish_rate_per_min: 5
  tenant_max_credits: 100
  burst_slack_percent: 12
```

maria: queued requests consume a pending token (cheap) and only convert to a real slot lease when the runtime can assign gpu memory + kvcache. that conversion charges one credit.

raj: so pending tokens don't block other tenants' future prewarms?

maria: right. pending tokens are soft and expire quickly; they don't reserve heavy resources. conversion has to respect headroom and admission policy.

liam: what about tenant fairness during flash surges? credits alone could let noisy tenants starve others.

maria: we keep a moving-window fairness score. admission = min(credit_score, fairness_score, bucket_headroom). fairness_score is computed from recent qps and successful conversions. if score too high -> temporary throttle.

kevin: how do we measure 'conversion' latency impact? we need observability hooks.

sophie: add metrics: lease_convert_time_ms, pending_token_expiry_count, credits_consumed, fairness_rejects. also trace span on conversion so traces show warmup vs actual generation.

maria: yes, proposed metric names: `redwood.lease.convert.latency_ms`, `redwood.lease.pending.expired`, `redwood.tenant.credits.used` 

devops-bot: deploy-notify: staging autoscaler-config updated by maria at 3776543300

raj: edge-case: if a node drains while conversions are in flight, do we rollback credits?

maria: good catch. plan: mark conversions as provisional until runtime confirms KV attached. provisional conversions decrement a provisional counter but not final credits. on success we decrement final credit and increment provisional->final metric. on rollback we refund to tenant_credit_pool.

liam: refund window bounded by `lease_cooldown_sec`? sounds ok. avoid double refunds.

kevin: what's default cooldown? 120s above. seems short for slow attaches on some HW. maybe make it adaptive based on attach latency percentile.

maria: thinking the same — config supports `lease_cooldown_policy: static|adaptive` and adaptive uses p90 attach_latency * 1.5 + base.

kevin: can we add safety to prevent abuse where tenant spends credits but never completes conversions (e.g., malformed requests)?

sophie: have a max-provisional-per-tenant counter and a per-request validation hook before conversion. invalid requests should fail fast and not consume provisional.

maria: operational flow for operator fallback: if operator detects global pressure (node shortage), switch to degraded admission mode: 1) disable provisional conversions, 2) raise soft eviction aggressiveness, 3) enable best-effort spill to cheaper model variants.

raj: operator needs a clear kill-switch and telemetry to justify fallback. should be a separate small-step rollout.

maria: agreed. we'll expose operator endpoints `/v1/operator/scale-mode` and `/v1/operator/evict-now` with audit logging.

liam: any implications for Dedicated SLA? evictions count against latency but not availability guarantees right? need SRE input.

kevin: doc that evictions are best-effort within dedicated pool SLO; for enterprise customers we can pin `hard_reserve=true` to skip soft eviction.

maria: good. pinning will bypass fairness and credit draws. note: pinned tenants still count towards capacity and reduce headroom for others.

kevin: what about pricing signals? credits map to billing units so any provisional refund affects billing accuracy. must ensure billing only finalizes on confirmed conversion.

sophie: yep billing event on finalization only. provisional changes not billed. add `billing.confirmation_latency_ms` metric.

maria: rollout plan: 1) unit tests + simulation harness for 5 traffic shapes, 2) canary on a small dedicated pool with `adaptive` cooldown off by default, 3) run 48h soak with an injected noisy-tenant test, 4) gather fairness/reject/convert metrics, 5) enable adaptive and iterate.

liam: simulation harness idea: reuse the existing `pool-sim` with added provisional state machine and attach-time distributions.

raj: I'll pair with QA on the noisy-tenant tests and add a chaos script to kill nodes mid-conversion.

kevin: one more: migration for existing pools — need a config migration path that doesn't flip defaults for customers.

maria: default preserve-mode = `compat` which keeps current behavior (no provisional, no credits). customers opt-in to new policy per-pool. good call.

sophie: can you file the RFC PR with config snippets + simulation results? I can review tests.

maria: will do. opening PR after addressing adaptive cooldown feedback. will drop a short design note in the docs repo too.

kevin: :thumbsup: thanks maria. this looks solid and pragmatic.

maria: thanks all. I'll ping again once PR is up.
